# Results — Study 884 (Convexity Barbell)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: a
**duration-matched barbell** (a mix of SHY and TLT weighted to the same empirical duration
as the IEF bullet) carries **more convexity** than the bullet, so at equal duration it
should out-earn the bullet when yields move a lot (the second-order term `+½·C·(Δy)²` is
bigger for the more convex book). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python
examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `32356eb6aefe` (four-ETF
close panel). Stamped run as-of 2026-06-30 — no partial months.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`), **SHY / IEF / TLT** (Treasury ladder) + **BIL** (T-bill cash), 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** overlapping rows |
| Bullet | **IEF** (7-10y Treasury) — the belly, 100% |
| Barbell | **w·SHY (1-3y) + (1-w)·TLT (20y+)**, `w` set each day so the barbell's empirical duration equals IEF's; mean weight **0.605·SHY / 0.395·TLT** |
| Rates factor | the **equal-weight mean** of the three bond daily returns; each bond's **empirical duration** = its trailing-252d beta to it |
| Duration match | `w·β_SHY + (1-w)·β_TLT = β_IEF` ⇒ `w = (β_TLT−β_IEF)/(β_TLT−β_SHY)`, from betas known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`, zero look-ahead) |
| Cash leg | **BIL**, used for the excess-vs-excess Sharpe race (both books minus BIL) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag (durations through close `t−1` → hold day `t`); the costed timer charges one-way cost × the barbell's daily rebalancing turnover (the bullet is buy-and-hold, ~zero turnover) |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample & Welch *t*; excess-vs-excess Sharpe; block-bootstrap mean CI; a convexity regression + smile; a two-era cut; a calendar-year table; a leg-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship / short-history — named on the Signal axis.** The three-bond ladder
(SHY/IEF/TLT) + BIL all trade continuously from before 2010, so nothing is silently
dropped, but restricting to this clean ladder is itself a design selection, disclosed here.

## The duration ladder — betas rise monotonically with maturity

| bond | SHY (1-3y) | IEF (7-10y) | TLT (20y+) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| avg trailing-252d β to the rates factor (empirical duration) | 0.116 | 0.864 | 2.020 |

The factor cleanly orders the curve; solving `w·β_SHY + (1-w)·β_TLT = β_IEF` gives a
barbell of ≈ **60.5% SHY / 39.5% TLT** that matches the bullet's first-order rate exposure
(the spread's residual duration slope is **+0.009**, i.e. ≈ 0 — matched).

## The headline — duration-matched barbell vs the IEF bullet

Daily total return, n = **3,894** days:

| book | ann. return | ann. vol | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **barbell** (0.605·SHY + 0.395·TLT) | **+2.15%/yr** | 6.41% | −23.5% |
| **bullet** (IEF) | **+2.28%/yr** | 6.52% | −23.9% |

The two are 0.944-correlated (duration-matched). The barbell does **not** out-earn the
bullet — it earns *slightly less* at essentially the same volatility and drawdown:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (barbell − bullet)** | **−0.054 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **−0.27** |
| one-sample *t* | −0.25 |
| spread Sharpe | −0.06 |
| bootstrap spread-mean CI95 | **[−0.433, +0.344] bps** (straddles zero) |
| **excess-vs-excess Sharpe** (both minus BIL) | barbell **+0.147** vs bullet **+0.165** → advantage **−0.018** (Welch *t* = −0.06) |

The spread is indistinguishable from zero and, if anything, marginally negative: **no edge.**

## Convexity — the mechanical claim vs the tape

Regress the daily spread on `[1, f, f²]` (`f` = rates factor). Analytically the barbell
*is* more convex — it holds the two wings, whose price/yield curvature at equal duration
exceeds the belly's. But on the realized total-return tape the convexity does **not** show
up as a spread that rises with the squared rate move:

| quantity | value | claim |
|---|--:|:--|
| convexity slope on `f²` | **−0.222** | should be **> 0** if the barbell captures its extra convexity — it is **wrong-signed** |
| mean-spread split | convexity part −0.047 + carry/drift −0.007 bps | — |

**Convexity smile** — mean spread (bps/day) by absolute-rate-move quintile (small → big):

| |move| bucket | [0] small | [1] | [2] | [3] | [4] big |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| mean spread (bps) | +0.305 | +0.014 | +0.053 | −0.693 | +0.052 |

No monotone rise into the big-move bucket — the barbell does **not** systematically
out-earn the bullet when yields move most. The textbook convexity smile is absent.

## The 2022 tell — the biggest rate move in the sample

| year | barbell | bullet | spread |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2021 | −1.46% | −3.33% | **+1.89%** |
| **2022** (historic selloff) | **−15.40%** | **−15.16%** | **−0.38%** |
| 2025 (long-end selloff) | +4.79% | +8.03% | **−3.06%** |

In 2022 — the largest "yields move a lot" event in decades, exactly the scenario the claim
says the barbell should win — the duration-matched barbell **under-performed** the bullet.
The extra convexity was more than offset by non-parallel curve moves (the long wing selling
off harder than a parallel shift implies) that the belly bullet does not carry.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,760) | +0.034 bps | +0.11 | +0.04 |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −0.126 bps | −0.47 | −0.14 |

Flat-to-slightly-negative in both eras. Never a real edge.

## Placebo — is even the (near-zero) spread a convexity alignment?

Keep the duration-match weights but read each barbell leg's return from an independently
time-permuted copy (breaking the day-by-day alignment), 400 draws:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | −0.054 bps |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.129 bps (0.061) |
| right-tail p | 0.122 |

The observed sits *inside* the placebo cloud (not in the right tail): there is no
convexity-alignment signal to speak of.

## The timer — nothing to harvest, and costs only subtract

The barbell turns over slowly (mean L1 turnover ≈ 0.0037/day — the belly-match weight
drifts gently), so costs are tiny; but the gross spread is already ≈ 0, so the net is
negative at every cost level.

| one-way cost | gross/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.5 bp | −0.054 bps | **−0.056 bps** | −0.25 | −0.07 | −0.14%/yr |
| 1 bp | −0.054 bps | **−0.057 bps** | −0.26 | −0.07 | −0.14%/yr |
| 2 bps | −0.054 bps | **−0.061 bps** | −0.28 | −0.07 | −0.15%/yr |

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded three-bond curve with a planted duration ladder and an **exaggerated**
convexity ladder (`C ∝ D²`, disclosed as stylised) plus a carry curve. `edge = 0` = the
null: convexity is present but exactly paid for by a yield give-up ⇒ zero net spread.
`edge > 0` = convexity **underpriced** ⇒ a real net pickup. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* | convexity slope |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.01** (sd 0.73), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20** | +0.70 (structural, in every world) |
| planted (`edge = 0.6` bps/day, seed 884) | **+4.30** | +0.70 |

The detector recovers a *planted* under-priced-convexity edge cleanly and almost never
fires on the null, while the convexity slope is positive in *both* worlds (convexity is a
structural property, an edge only when under-priced). So the real-tape null is a genuine
absence of a *net* convexity edge, not a broken engine. *(A faithful-engine / power check
only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** A duration-matched SHY+TLT barbell does **not** out-earn the IEF
  bullet. The spread is **−0.054 bps/day** (NW *t* = **−0.27**), its bootstrap CI straddles
  zero **[−0.43, +0.34]**, the excess-vs-excess Sharpe advantage is **−0.02**, and it is
  flat in both eras. The convexity the barbell genuinely carries is invisible in total
  return: the `f²` slope is **wrong-signed (−0.22)**, the convexity smile is absent, and in
  2022's historic selloff — the very "big move" the claim needs — the barbell
  **under-performed**. The market prices convexity into the wings' yield give-up, and the
  barbell pays for it with butterfly (curve-reshaping) risk the bullet avoids. The 20-seed
  synthetic control recovers a *planted* edge cleanly, so the machinery is sound — the net
  edge is simply absent.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no gross edge to cost: the spread is ≈ 0 before
  frictions and negative after even the tiny rebalancing cost (net ~ −0.14%/yr). The
  "free convexity lunch" is a mirage — fully offset by carry give-up and curve risk.
